extracted.intended_audience: aspiring novelists; critics and students of fiction
extracted.subtask_description: General practical and critical guidance on composing novels and fiction, emphasizing principles of realism, freedom, workmanship, and the relation of story and form. Intended to guide the novelist’s choices about subject, method, and execution rather than provide rigid rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be interesting
rubrics_metrics.description: The only obligation to which in advance we may hold a novel ... is that it be interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: James repeatedly asserts that 'being interesting' is the sole universal obligation; everything a novelist does should aim to interest the reader. This is the minimal prescriptive standard—beyond it, freedom of method applies. If a work fails to interest, other merits are moot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of choice / avoid prescriptive rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The novel lives upon exercise, and the very meaning of exercise is freedom; to mark it out by prescription injures it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: James warns against laying down strict beforehand rules (formulas about plot, tone, 'modern English novel', etc.). He treats a priori injunctions as limiting the novelist’s experimentation and development. The form should be appreciated after the fact; authors must be free to choose subjects and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: The novel must compete with life (illusion of life)
rubrics_metrics.description: The only reason for the existence of a novel is that it does compete with life ... as the picture is reality, so the novel is history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The novel should not apologize for being 'make believe' but should present itself with the assurance and authority of history or painting. The art’s aim is to render the look and meaning of things, producing an illusion of life that allows it to 'compete' with other arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air of reality / truth of detail (exactness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The air of reality (solidity of specification) seems to me to be the supreme virtue of a novel—the merit on which all its other merits ... depend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exactness and truthful particulars are essential: realistic, specific detail creates the illusion of life. James links this to careful workmanship and to taking notes; lack of detail undermines other qualities such as moral purpose or character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write from experience (impressions rather than narrow biography)
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelist must write from his experience ... experience consists of impressions; impressions are experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: James qualifies 'experience' broadly: not only personal biography but impressions, glimpses, imaginative inferences ('the power to guess the unseen from the seen'). A novelist should cultivate sensibility—'be one of the people on whom nothing is lost'—so that even fleeting things become usable material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take notes / cultivate observation
rubrics_metrics.description: He bids him take notes. He cannot possibly take too many, he cannot possibly take enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: James endorses keeping notes/commonplace book and persistent observation as the raw material of realistic fiction, while acknowledging there is no handbook that can prescribe exactly what notes to take; selection of notes is the novelist’s life-work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters must be clear in outline but achieved by execution
rubrics_metrics.description: One’s figures should be clear in outline ... how he shall make them so is a secret between his good angel and himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity of character is crucial, but James rejects formulaic methods (over-description, tricks, or purely dialogue-driven prescriptions). Clarity comes from the author’s manner and execution; it cannot be reliably taught as a recipe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not betray the fiction (avoid apologetic asides)
rubrics_metrics.description: A novelist betrays a sacred office when, in a digression or aside, he concedes to the reader that he and this trusting friend are only 'making believe.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: James condemns narrative asides that break the illusion by telling readers the events are contrived; such apologies deprive the novelist of standing-room and undermine the work’s seriousness (example: Trollope's frequent concessions). Maintain narrative authority and the illusion of reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution / workmanship / style is paramount
rubrics_metrics.description: It is almost impossible to estimate too highly the value of careful workmanship—that is, of style ... It is of execution that we are talking—that being the only point of a novel that is open to contention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the subject/idea (donnée) matters, critical judgment properly applies to what the author makes of it. The quality of phrasing, the control of tone, and the style determine success; execution is the primary criterion critics can assess.

rubrics_metrics.name: The story (idea/donnée) matters but is inseparable from form
rubrics_metrics.description: The story represents the subject, the idea, the data of the novel ... every word and every punctuation-point contribute directly to the expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: James rejects strict separations of 'story' vs 'treatment'; the idea permeates form and vice versa. A workable starting-point is necessary, but the distinction collapses in a successful work where idea and form are integrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpenetration of description, dialogue, and incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition does not exist in a series of blocks ... a passage of description that is not in its intention narrative, a passage of dialogue that is not in its intention descriptive ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating description, dialogue, and incident as isolated categories. In good fiction they melt into each other and each part often performs several functions (narrative, descriptive, illustrative). Beware critics who rigidly separate 'novel of incident' vs 'novel of character.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection should be typical and inclusive (don't prettify or censor life)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is essentially selection, but it is a selection whose main care is to be typical, to be inclusive ... it is all experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection must aim to represent life broadly, including disagreeable or painful elements; artistic selection is not merely picking prettiness. James argues against moralistic restrictions that banish the ugly or painful from literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid artificial rearrangement; capture the irregular rhythm of life
rubrics_metrics.description: Catching the very note and trick, the strange irregular rhythm of life, that is the attempt whose strenuous force keeps Fiction upon her feet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: James criticizes overly contrived arrangements and conventional 'tricks' that distance fiction from the texture of lived experience. The novelist should seek naturalness and the surprising rhythms of reality rather than stylized contrivances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge the work by its chosen data (respect the artist’s starting-point)
rubrics_metrics.description: I judge you by what you propose, and you must look out for me there ... I have the standard; I judge you by what you propose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical evaluation should accept the author's chosen subject as given and evaluate the success of execution. Critics should not prescriptively forbid subjects; instead they should measure whether the artist has made the proposed idea interesting and well-executed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth/quality of the author's mind supplies moral seriousness
rubrics_metrics.description: The deepest quality of a work of art will always be the quality of the mind of the producer ... No good novel will ever proceed from a superficial mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than an imposed 'conscious moral purpose,' James contends that moral force in fiction arises from the richness and nobility of the author’s mind. A profound, informed intelligence in the author covers the moral ground necessary in art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not confine subjects to a writer’s social station without reason
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer whose friends and personal experiences belong to the lower middle-class should carefully avoid introducing his characters into Society'—this injunction is chilling; imagination can enable truthful portrayals beyond immediate experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: James rejects strict social or biographical limits on subject matter; with observation, imagination, and the power to 'guess the unseen from the seen,' writers from varied backgrounds can authentically treat subjects outside their personal milieu (example: the country damsel plausibly imagining garrison life).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner is personal and largely incommunicable
rubrics_metrics.description: His manner is his secret, not necessarily a deliberate one. He cannot disclose it, as a general thing, if he would; he would be at a loss to teach it to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While technical rudiments can be taught and studied, the novelist's distinctive manner—tone, vision, particular execution—often cannot be prescribed. Teachers can point to models, but personal manner emerges from practice and temperament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be generous, delicate, and strive for completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that your first duty is to be as complete as possible—to make as perfect a work. Be generous and delicate, and then, in the vulgar phrase, go in!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: James counsels the aspiring novelist toward striving for perfection: generosity of spirit, delicacy of treatment, and thoroughness in execution. This is both an aesthetic and ethical injunction about the author's attitude toward subject and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect variety of taste and accept that liking remains ultimate test
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing will ever take the place of the good old fashion of 'liking' a work of art or not liking it; the primitive, that ultimate, test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: James acknowledges that despite rules and criticism, personal taste is decisive. Critics and writers should accept differences of preference (different readers favor different subjects and treatments). Selection by readers will follow experience and taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow art to experiment (value of unsuccessful experiments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of the most interesting experiments of which it is capable are hidden in the bosom of common things ... Flaubert has written a story about the devotion of a servant-girl to a parrot ... we are perfectly free to find it flat, but I think it might have been interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: James argues that even unsuccessful or odd experiments are valuable contributions to knowledge about what can be done in fiction. Writers should be encouraged to attempt unusual subjects or forms; failure can still be instructive and important to the art’s development.
